data.title: Andy Burnham Weighs UK Strategy Toward EU as Canada and EU Draft Broad Pact
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is weighing his strategy toward the EU as Canada and the EU draft a comprehensive agreement covering trade and security. The EU and Canada are working to build a new kind of partnership to counter the United States, which could overshadow the UK-EU summit planned for November. Burnham has begun outlining his European policy, seeking closer ties with the EU while addressing concerns about the impact of the EU's "Made in Europe" plan on British industry.

data.title: Former NYC Deputy Mayor Edward Skyler Reflects on 9/11 Aftermath
data.description:
Edward Skyler said it was extremely difficult to make decisions after 9/11, when 2,700 people were murdered and New York was filled with grief, anxiety and political tension, according to Bloomberg.

He said smoke was still rising from the World Trade Center site when Mayor Bloomberg was sworn in on 01/01/2002, after the economic damage had already been done. Skyler said city leaders had to listen to all sides and make a plan that served New York’s best interests, even if it disappointed some people, and said those decisions have stood the test of time.

data.title: Peskov Says Russia, U.S., and Ukraine May Hold Trilateral Talks Soon
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Russian presidential spokesman Dmitry Peskov said in an interview on September 11 local time that the Kremlin expects Russia, the United States, and Ukraine to hold trilateral talks soon and continue dialogue. He added that there are no preconditions for negotiations on the Ukraine issue itself, and that Russia remains open to talks.

data.title: Jim Cramer Says Falling Oil Prices Lifted Stocks, Warns Fed Meeting Could Shift Outlook
data.description:
According to CNBC, Jim Cramer said falling oil prices helped revive stocks on Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 509 points, or 0.98%, the S&P 500 up 0.86%, and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% after four straight down sessions. He said positive after-hours results from Adobe and Oracle helped lift technology shares and renewed interest in enterprise software and data center stocks, naming Dell, Vertiv, Cisco, Marvell, GE Vernova and Hewlett Packard Enterprise as possible beneficiaries.

Cramer said next week’s market direction will depend largely on oil prices and interest rates, with the war in Iran a key variable. He said progress toward peace could push oil lower and ease inflation pressure, while renewed fighting could send oil higher and hurt stocks. He also said the Federal Reserve’s Open Market Committee meets Wednesday and that the consensus expects policymakers to raise rates to combat persistent inflation. Cramer said he will watch how longer-term Treasury yields react and warned that another rate increase would make investing more difficult. He also said Lennar reports after Wednesday’s close, while Brinker International and Intuit hold analyst meetings Thursday.

data.title: JPMorgan Ends Lending Relationship With Situational Awareness After Losses
data.description: According to Sina Finance, citing the Financial Times and people familiar with the matter, JPMorgan Chase has stopped providing loans to Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund, Situational Awareness. JPMorgan had previously financed the fund through its prime brokerage business and was one of its main lenders. After the fund posted losses, JPMorgan told it that the lending relationship would end. Morgan Stanley has been in contact with Situational Awareness since its launch but never established a banking relationship. The Financial Times said JPMorgan, Situational Awareness, and Morgan Stanley all declined to comment.

data.title: U.S. Appeals Court Rejects Energy Department Bid to Block Michigan Coal Plant Closure
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit ruled that the Energy Department had no authority under federal law to use emergency powers to stop the closure of Michigan's J.H. Campbell coal-fired power plant. The court sided with Michigan, Minnesota, Illinois, and public-interest groups, saying the Energy Department misread the law's meaning of "emergency intervention" and that there was no short-term crisis overriding state governments' grid-management authority.
